run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:18:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert fires because frontend-proxy has been emitting a small but steady stream of error spans on its 'ingress' operation since 2026-11-18T00:55-ish (first non-zero 5m rate at 2026-11-18T23:55:47Z), reaching 0.0111/s at 00:19:00Z, exactly the value in the alert annotation. The error spans are backed by frontend-proxy's own access log: every observed failure is '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward upstream 'frontend' (100.96.2.11:8080), with upstream service time '-', i.e. the frontend side closed the connection before a response started. No other otel-demo service shows a sustained error rate, the frontend itself records zero error spans, its latency distribution is flat, its pod has 0 restarts and no memory/CPU pressure. The only fault-injection setting that is switched on anywhere I could read is flagd-config flag 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' (defaultVariant 'on', value 100, description 'Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests'), and the load-generator Deployment was rolled out at 00:09:37Z with a pod template identical to the previous ReplicaSet apart from a restartedAt annotation. However the declared flood itself is NOT visible (GET / stayed ~0.3/s) and the change-history integration is not available, so the causal link and the activation time of the flag remain unverified; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans on span_name 'ingress' were 0/s at 23:49:47-23:54:47Z, became non-zero at 23:55:47Z (0.0037/s), peaked at 0.0259/s around 00:01-00:03 and were 0.0111/s at 00:19:00Z - the same value the alert annotation reports as current (0.01111111111111111).

Among all services, only frontend-proxy shows a sustained error-span rate; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show only isolated single-span blips (max 0.00437/s) and accounting, frontend and payment are 0 across 23:49:47-00:27:47Z.

frontend-proxy access-log lines show the failures as 503 with code 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0, /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z, /api/data/?contextKeys=telescopes, /api/products/1YMWWN1N4O, / and /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO, with upstream 'frontend' 100.96.2.11:8080 and upstream service time '-'; 10 such lines were read between 23:54:40.642Z and 00:02:52.352Z (read cut at the 4 MiB limit at 00:06:46Z).

The same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern continues after the load-generator rollout: 9 such lines between 00:10:39.307Z and 00:22:26.650Z (GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, /api/recommendations, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel, /api/cart, /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/66VCHSJNUP, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/data/?contextKeys=books, /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM), all toward upstream 'frontend' 100.96.2.11:8080.

Latency did not shift: the share of frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' spans (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) under 1000 ms stayed between 0.972 and 0.987 for every 2-minute point from 23:49 to 00:27Z, including before and after the error onset.
The frontend service records STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 for its GET spans (and 0 for the service as a whole) while its GET span rate held at 9.0-10.0/s from 23:56 to 00:26Z.

frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, started 2026-11-17T23:37:49Z) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth (started 23:37:48Z) are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last-terminated state.

Resource readings: frontend container peak working set 131,723,264 bytes against a 200Mi limit, frontend CPU usage ~0.05 cores with CFS throttle ratio 0.23-0.25 at 00:25-00:27Z; frontend-proxy container peak working set 20,934,656 bytes against a 50Mi limit with throttle ratio 0.035-0.067.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json in which flag 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' is state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'on' (variants off=0, on=100) and description 'Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests.', while adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak(off=0), imageSlowLoad(off=0), kafkaQueueProblems(off=0), paymentFailure(off=0), paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all have defaultVariant 'off'.

Deployment load-generator was rolled out at 00:09:37Z: ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd (revision 2) was created with a pod template identical to load-generator-57ffcd644 (revision 1) except the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation, and pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 was killed at 00:09:38Z (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet events up/down, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete).

No homepage flood is visible: frontend span_name 'GET /' held 0.27-0.37/s from 00:15 to 00:25Z while total frontend span activity was ~10/s, and load-generator logged 'User accessing index page' at roughly that same low rate (287 matching lines up to 00:23:33Z in a ~14 minute window).
Error onset coincides with the load ramp reaching its plateau: frontend GET span rate rose from 2.5/s at 23:49Z to ~9-10/s by 23:56Z and stayed flat, and the first 503 was logged at 23:54:40.642Z.

The 503s originate on the frontend side, not in frontend-proxy: the access-log detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream host 100.96.2.11:8080 (frontend) and no upstream service time means the frontend closed the TCP connection before sending response headers, so frontend-proxy answered 503 and the aborted requests produced no completed frontend span (hence frontend's zero error rate).

The fault-injection setting in effect is ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config flag 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' = 'on' (value 100, 'Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests.'): it is the only fault switch that is on, it names the frontend that is terminating connections, no other object was seen applying a fault, and the load-generator Deployment was restarted at 00:09:37Z with an unchanged pod template. Its declared effect (a homepage flood) was not observed, so this remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated mechanism.

Alternative mechanism for the sporadic connection_termination: a keep-alive race between the frontend's own connection idle timeout and frontend-proxy's reused upstream connections, whose frequency grows with connection-pool size as concurrency rises - consistent with the onset at the traffic plateau and with the ~0.5 errors/minute steady rate, but not verifiable from the available telemetry (envoy cluster/upstream timing config and frontend server timeouts were not readable).

Rejected as the cause: resource exhaustion of frontend-proxy (limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi). Its CFS throttle ratio stayed 0.035-0.067, working set peaked at 20.9 MB of 50Mi, the pod never restarted, and the 503 pattern was unchanged across the window.

Rejected as the cause: a failing or slow downstream dependency (product-catalog, cart, currency, checkout, payment, ad, recommendation). Those services show no sustained error spans (only isolated single-span blips for ad/fraud-detection/recommendation) and the sub-1000 ms share of frontend-proxy egress spans did not drop.

The frontend pod itself shows none of the usual damage markers: 0 restarts, no last-terminated reason, memory 131.7 MB of 200Mi, CFS throttle ~0.23-0.25 throughout (including before the error onset at 23:48), and 97-98% of completed proxy->frontend spans under 1 s, so the 503s are not explained by a frontend-wide outage, restart or latency collapse.

Verify the flagd flag history/audit for 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' (it is set to 'on' in otel-demo/flagd-config) and, as a test, switch its defaultVariant to 'off' and confirm whether the frontend-proxy 503 UC errors stop; also confirm whether flagd is actually serving 'on' to the load-generator and whether a homepage-flood task is spawned.

Compare the frontend server's keep-alive/idle timeouts with frontend-proxy's upstream HTTP/1 connection-pool idle timeout (and consider enabling retry on the frontend cluster), since the observed failure is 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on reused connections rather than a slow or erroring response.

gaps: Change-history integration is not available in this Run, so I cannot tell when flag 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' was switched to 'on' in otel-demo/flagd-config, nor whether that ConfigMap was edited around the 23:54Z error onset.

The declared fault of that flag (a homepage flood) was not observed: frontend 'GET /' stayed ~0.27-0.37/s and load-generator 'User accessing index page' ~0.3/s, so the causal link between the flag and the 503 UC errors is unverified.

Jaeger's stored traces end at about 2026-11-17T23:52:05Z (before the first 503 at 23:54:40Z); searches inside 00:18:18-00:18:25Z returned no traces, so no trace of any failing request exists to confirm which span/operation broke.
The frontend container wrote no log lines in 00:00-00:28Z (both streams read 0 bytes), so the application-side reason for the closed connections could not be read.
frontend-proxy log reads were cut by the 4 MiB limit (through 00:06:46Z and 00:23:33Z respectively), so the 5xx counts cited are lower bounds, not totals.
A query for 4xx access-log lines in 00:10-00:28Z returned no matching rows (no_data view); it is therefore not cited as proof that no 4xx occurred.

The Prometheus rules query by exact rule_name 'RequestErrorRate' returned nothing, so the alert's expression/threshold was not verified from the rule definition (the annotation's 'current' value does match the measured ingress error-span rate).
The trigger of the load-generator Deployment rollout at 00:09:37Z (kubectl restartedAt) and of the flagd rollout at 23:39:30Z could not be attributed to any observed actor or object.
next_steps: Inspect the otel-demo flagd flag-change audit/logs and the GitOps/Helm release history for otel-demo/flagd-config to date the 'loadGeneratorFloodHomepage' change.
Read frontend-proxy's full access log and envoy cluster config (upstream idle timeout, retries, max requests per connection) to validate or discard the keep-alive race hypothesis.
Check the frontend (Next.js) server-side keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout configuration and any node/undici connection-limit settings.
Extend frontend-proxy log collection past the 4 MiB read limit and aggregate 5xx per minute to quantify the real error volume behind RequestErrorRate.
